answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an economy uses game-theoretic multi-agent auditing paired with stake slashing and topological cut verifications. Auditing agents inspect cluster boundaries like inspectors at a timber processing wharf: if an isolated agent grove cannot prove independent paths across graph cuts, its bonded stake is slashed. Because multi-agent cross-verification scales exponentially in cost with attacker cluster size, fake identities become prohibitively expensive to maintain.
